junction.name: Francis Lewis Boulevard & 243 Street, New York City

claims.text: Francis Lewis Boulevard & 243 Street had 0 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 pedestrians injured, 0 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Francis Lewis Boulevard & 243 Street's own: the city's record places 110 of the 123 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's priority junctions.
Held up on later years: a vehicle was making left turn in 35% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 15% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for S CONDUIT AVE (NY 27), Francis Lewis Boulevard, 243 Street (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 31, New York City Council; Queens Community Board 13.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
